title: Coming and going: ていく and てくる
summary: 来る always moves toward where the speaker is, 行く away from it. Attached to a て-form they describe change in space, in time and in how you feel.

blocks.text: **来る** can only mean moving from somewhere the speaker is **not** to the place where the speaker **is** (in mind as well). **行く** is looser: it moves away, or between two places the speaker is not at. That is why you cannot tell someone on the phone "I'll come to you" with 来る: you say 行く.
With a て-form, the helper keeps the same direction. 持って**くる** brings something toward me; 持って**いく** takes it away. Then the picture stretches to **time** and to **feeling**.

blocks.en: I'll take a lunch (away from here).
It has started to rain. (rain came toward the present)

blocks.jp: これからも日本語を勉強していく。
blocks.en: I will keep studying Japanese from now on. (moving forward in time)

blocks.text: **くる** is also a movement toward **my own state of mind**. 分かる means "be clear", so as you study, math *comes* to be clear to you. And **〜てきた** sounds like the change touches me or us, while **〜ていった** reports it from outside.

blocks.jp: だんだん数学が分かってくる。
blocks.en: Math gradually becomes clear to me.
It has been getting colder lately. (I feel it)

items: **来る**: toward the speaker's place, time or state. **行く**: away from it.
**〜てくる**: change arriving toward now; **〜ていく**: change continuing away, into the future.
**くる** can be subjective (it touches me); **いく** can be objective.
There are no strict rules: use the picture, and let immersion fill it in.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: 友達の家に行くとき、ケーキを持って＿＿。
questions.en: When I go to my friend's house, I'll take a cake.
questions.note: The cake moves away from here, so いく.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: 友達が私の家に来て、ケーキを持って＿＿。
questions.en: My friend came to my house and brought a cake.
questions.note: The cake arrives where the speaker is, so くる.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.en: Oh, it has started to snow.
questions.note: The change arrives toward the present moment: てくる.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: これからも毎日走って＿＿つもりだ。
questions.en: I intend to keep running every day from now on.
questions.note: Moving forward in time is ていく.

questions.instruction: Which sentence says "I will keep doing my best from now on"?
options: これからもがんばってくる。
これからもがんばっていく。
これからもがんばってしまう。
これからもがんばっておく。
questions.note: ていく carries an action forward in time.

questions.instruction: On the phone, which verb do you use to say you are heading to your friend's house?
questions.prompt: 今から、あなたの家に＿＿よ。
questions.en: I'm heading to your place now.
questions.note: 来る only moves to where the speaker is.

questions.instruction: What does 来る point toward?
options: Toward the speaker's place, time or state
Between two places the speaker is not at
questions.note: 来る always comes toward the speaker's side.

questions.instruction: What does 〜ていく show about a change?
options: It continues away, into the future
questions.note: いく is movement away from now.

questions.instruction: Tap the helper verb that brings the change toward me
questions.en: I have become gradually better (and I feel it).
questions.note: きた: the change reached my own state.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that points the movement away from here
questions.en: My younger brother left, taking his bag.
questions.note: 〜ていった moves away from the speaker.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.note: て-form + いく: carry it away from here.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.note: てきた: the change has reached the present.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: Gradually English is becoming clear to me.
questions.en: Gradually English is becoming clear to me.
questions.note: くる is also movement toward my own state of mind.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: I will keep running every day (from now on).
questions.en: I will keep running every day (from now on).
questions.note: ていく continues the action forward in time.

questions.instruction: True or false? 〜てくる can describe a change that reaches the speaker's own feeling.
questions.note: くる can be a movement toward my state of mind.

questions.instruction: Which means "bring (toward me)"?
questions.note: て-form + くる keeps the direction toward the speaker.

questions.instruction: Which sounds like the change touches me or us?
questions.note: 〜ていった reports it from outside.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: 友達が遠くから歩いて＿＿＿。
questions.en: My friend came walking from far away.
questions.note: The friend moves toward the speaker.

questions.instruction: Why can you not say 来るよ on the phone when you are heading to the other person's house?
options: 来る only moves toward where the speaker is
来る is for the past only
questions.note: Use 行く when going to the other person's place.

questions.instruction: In 日本語が分かってくる, what is くる picturing?
options: Understanding arriving toward my own state of mind
questions.note: Clarity comes toward me as I study.

questions.instruction: True or false? There are strict rules for ていく and てくる, so you must memorize them.
questions.note: Use the picture of direction and let immersion fill in the rest.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: 春になって、だんだんあたたかく＿＿。
questions.en: With spring here, it has gradually gotten warmer.
questions.note: A change reaching the present is てきた.
